---
title: "Evaluation"
---

A fitted model is useful only if it performs well on new observations. These
materials develop the tools for evaluating, comparing, and selecting models
without mistaking a good fit to training data for reliable future performance.

We continue to use the gas-turbine emissions measurements, but shift the
question from *how do we fit a model?* to *how do we assess one fairly?*

## 1. Polynomial regression and overfitting

**Estimated time:** 25–35 minutes

Fit linear, moderately flexible, and high-degree polynomial models to a
limited turbine calibration sample. Compare training and test RMSE and
$R^2$ to see why a flexible model can fit training observations well while
predicting new observations poorly.

[View the notebook](01-polynomial-model-validation.ipynb)

## 2. Ridge and Lasso regularization

**Estimated time:** 30–45 minutes

Use 75 gas-turbine operating observations to see how Ridge and Lasso
regularization control a fixed set of measured operating features. Compare
training and validation RMSE across penalty strengths, then contrast Ridge's
coefficient shrinkage with Lasso's exact-zero feature selection.

[View the notebook](02-ridge-regularization.ipynb)

## 3. Tuning decision-tree complexity

**Estimated time:** 25–35 minutes

Use the gas-turbine positive/negative CO-emission label to compare decision
trees of different complexity. Tune maximum depth and minimum leaf size with
a fixed train/test split, then use ROC AUC to see why a fully grown tree can
fit the training set perfectly while generalizing poorly.

[View the notebook](03-decision-tree-hyperparameter-tuning.ipynb)
